chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Aqeeqa is on the seventh day, and the midwife is given the leg along with the thigh, and the bone is not broken.

key_terms.الرِّجْلُ: The leg: A specific part of the animal given to the midwife
key_terms.الْعَظْمُ: The bone: The skeletal structure which should remain intact during slaughter
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa: The sacrificial animal offered for a newborn child
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةَ: The midwife: The woman who assisted in childbirth
key_terms.الْوَرِكِ: The thigh: The upper part of the leg, often mentioned alongside the leg
key_terms.يَوْمَ السَّابِعِ: The seventh day: The prescribed time for the Aqeeqa ritual

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rulings and timing for performing Aqeeqa for a newborn in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of performing the Aqeeqa on the seventh day, a practice deeply rooted in the Prophet's tradition and emphasized in Shia jurisprudence as a means of expressing gratitude for the newborn. It provides specific practical details, such as gifting the midwife a portion of the meat (specifically the leg with the thigh) and the recommendation against breaking the bones, which signifies respect and completeness in the ritual offering.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya Bin Adam, from Al Kahly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Aqeeqa is on the seventh day, and give the mid-wife the leg (of the slaughtered animal) along with the leaf (of silver or gold), and do not break the bone’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from his father from Zakariya ibn Adam from al-Kahiliy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

On the seventh day from the birth of a child ‘Aqiqah must be offered. One leg and hip of the animal offered as ‘Aqiqah should be given to al-Qabilah (the special nurse, doctor) and the bones should not be broken.’”
